overview:
Get metrics from Microsoft Active Directory to visualize and monitor its performances.

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.0.0
setup:
### Installation

The Agent's Active Directory check is included in the [Datadog Agent][1] package, so you don't need to install anything else on your servers.

If installing the Datadog Agent on a domain environment, see [the installation requirements for the Agent][2]

### Configuration

#### Metric collection

1. Edit the `active_directory.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your [Agent's configuration directory][3] to start collecting your Active Directory performance data. The default setup should already collect metrics for the localhost. See the [sample active_directory.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][5]

**Note**: Use version 4.4.0 or later of this check to collect the latest metrics.

#### Service checks
Datadog recommends enabling the [Windows Services][10] integration to also monitor the state of the Active Directory services.

Example configuration:
```yaml
instances:
  - services:
    - ntds
    - netlogon
    - dhcp
    - dfsr
    - adws
    - kdc
```

**Note:** The Datadog Agent might not have access to all the services (e.g. NTDS). See [Service permissions][11] for more information to grant access.

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][7] and look for `active_directory` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: active_directory.dfsr.conflict_space_in_use
metrics.description: The total size (in bytes) of conflict files generated during DFS replication..

metrics.name: active_directory.dfsr.deleted_space_in_use
metrics.description: The total size (in bytes) of files that have been deleted but are still in the staging folder.

metrics.name: active_directory.dfsr.file_installs_retried
metrics.description: The total number of file installations that required retry during DFS replication.

metrics.name: active_directory.dfsr.staging_space_in_use
metrics.description: The current size (in bytes) of the DFS replication staging folder.

metrics.name: active_directory.dhcp.failover.binding_updates_dropped
metrics.description: The number of DHCP binding update messages dropped.

metrics.name: active_directory.dhcp.failover.binding_updates_pending
metrics.description: The number of pending DHCP failover update messages.

metrics.name: active_directory.dhcp.failover.binding_updates_received
metrics.description: The number of DHCP failover update messages received (per second) from the failover partner.

metrics.name: active_directory.dhcp.failover.binding_updates_sent
metrics.description: The number of DHCP failover update messages sent (per second) to the failover partner.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.bytes.after_compression
metrics.description: The compressed size (in bytes) of compressed replication data inbound from directory system agents (DSAs) in other sites (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.bytes.before_compression
metrics.description: The uncompressed size (in bytes) of compressed replication data inbound from DSAs in other sites (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.bytes.not_compressed
metrics.description: The uncompressed size (in bytes) of replication data that was not compressed at the source - that is, inbound from other DSAs in the same site (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.bytes.total
metrics.description: The total number of bytes (per second) received through replication. It is the sum of the number of bytes of uncompressed data (never compressed) and compressed data (after compression).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.objects.applied_persec
metrics.description: The number of objects received (per second) from replication partners and applied by the local directory service. This counter excludes changes that are received but not applied (for example, when the update is already made). This counter indicates how many replication updates are occurring on the server as a result of changes generated on other servers.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.objects.filtered_persec
metrics.description: The number of objects received (per second) from replication partners that contained no updates that needed to be applied.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.objects.persec
metrics.description: The number of objects received (per second) through inbound replication from replication partners.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.objects.remaining
metrics.description: The number of objects remaining until the full synchronization process is completed.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.objects.remaining_in_packet
metrics.description: The number of object updates received in the current directory replication update packet that have not yet been applied to the local server. This counter tells you whether the monitored server is receiving changes, but is taking a long time applying them to the database.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.properties.applied_persec
metrics.description: The number of changes (per second) to object properties that are applied through inbound replication as a result of reconciliation logic.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.properties.filtered_persec
metrics.description: The number of changes (per second) to object properties received during the replication that are already made.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.properties.total_persec
metrics.description: The total number of changes (per second) to object properties received from replication partners.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.values.dns_persec
metrics.description: The number of values of object properties received (per second) from replication partners in which the values are for object properties that belong to distinguished names. This number includes objects that reference other objects. A high number from this counter might explain why inbound changes are slow to be applied to the database.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.inbound.values.total_persec
metrics.description: The total number of values of object properties received (per second) from replication partners. Each inbound object has one or more properties, and each property has zero or more values. A value of zero indicates that the property is to be removed.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.bytes.after_compression
metrics.description: The compressed size (in bytes) of compressed replication data that is outbound to DSAs in other sites (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.bytes.before_compression
metrics.description: The uncompressed size (in bytes) of compressed replication data outbound to DSAs in other sites (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.bytes.not_compressed
metrics.description: The uncompressed size (in bytes) of outbound replication data that was not compressed - that is, outbound to DSAs in the same site (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.bytes.total
metrics.description: The total number of bytes sent (per second). It is the sum of the number of bytes of uncompressed data (never compressed) and compressed data (after compression).

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.objects.filtered_persec
metrics.description: The number of objects (per second) acknowledged by outbound replication partners that required no updates. This counter includes objects that the outbound partner did not already have.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.objects.persec
metrics.description: The number of objects sent (per second) though outbound replication to replication partners.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.properties.persec
metrics.description: The number of properties sent (per second). This counter tells you whether a source server is returning objects or not. Sometimes, the server might stop working correctly and not return objects quickly or at all.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.values.dns_persec
metrics.description: The number values of object properties sent (per second) to replication partners in which the values are for object properties that belong to distinguished names.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.outbound.values.total_persec
metrics.description: The total number of values of object properties sent (per second), to replication partners.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.replication.pending_synchronizations
metrics.description: The number of directory synchronizations that are queued for this server that are not yet processed. This counter helps in determining replication backlog - the larger the number, the larger the backlog.

metrics.name: active_directory.dra.sync_requests_made
metrics.description: The number of synchronization requests made to replication partners since computer was last restarted.

metrics.name: active_directory.ds.client_binds_persec
metrics.description: The number of LDAP client bind operations (per second) including both successful and failed attempts.

metrics.name: active_directory.ds.threads_in_use
metrics.description: The current number of threads in use by the directory service (different from the number of threads in the directory service process). This counter represents the number of threads currently servicing API calls by clients, and you can use it to determine whether additional CPUs would be beneficial.

metrics.name: active_directory.ldap.active_threads
metrics.description: The current number of threads in use by the LDAP subsystem for processing requests.

metrics.name: active_directory.ldap.bind_time
metrics.description: The time (in milliseconds) required for the completion of the last successful LDAP binding.

metrics.name: active_directory.ldap.client_sessions
metrics.description: The number of sessions of connected LDAP clients.

metrics.name: active_directory.ldap.searches_persec
metrics.description: The number of search operations (per second) performed by LDAP clients.

metrics.name: active_directory.ldap.successful_binds_persec
metrics.description: The number of LDAP bindings (per second) that occurred successfully.

metrics.name: active_directory.ldap.writes_persec
metrics.description: The number of LDAP write operations performed (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.netlogon.semaphore_acquires
metrics.description: The total number of times the Netlogon semaphore has been obtained since system startup.

metrics.name: active_directory.netlogon.semaphore_hold_time
metrics.description: The average time (in seconds) that the Netlogon semaphore is held. High values indicate slow authentication processing.

metrics.name: active_directory.netlogon.semaphore_holders
metrics.description: The number of threads currently holding the Netlogon semaphore.

metrics.name: active_directory.netlogon.semaphore_timeouts
metrics.description: The total number of times a thread has timed out while waiting for the Netlogon semaphore.

metrics.name: active_directory.netlogon.semaphore_waiters
metrics.description: The number of threads waiting to obtain the Netlogon semaphore. A high value indicates authentication bottlenecks.

metrics.name: active_directory.security.kerberos_authentications
metrics.description: The number of Kerberos authentications processed (per second).

metrics.name: active_directory.security.ntlm_authentications
metrics.description: The number of NTLM authentications processed (per second).

monitors.title: LDAP binding duration is high
monitors.description: The binding process is crucial for authentication and authorization between a client and LDAP server. This monitor tracks the binding duration to indicate performance issues or delays in LDAP authentication or directory access.

monitors.title: Number of sessions for LDAP clients is anomalous
monitors.description: Sessions enable LDAP clients to interact with directory servers securely. This monitor detects anomalies in the number of client sessions in Active Directory LDAP to identify unusual activity or issues related to client sessions.
monitors.query: avg(last_12h):anomalies(avg:active_directory.ldap.client_sessions{*} by {host}, 'agile', 5, direction='both', alert_window='last_15m', interval=120, count_default_zero='true', seasonality='daily') >= 1

monitors.title: Number of LDAP bindings is anomalous
monitors.description: The binding operation ensures that only authenticated and authorized clients can access directory data. This monitor detects anomalies in the rate of successful LDAP binds per second in an Active Directory environment to identify unusual activity.
monitors.query: avg(last_12h):anomalies(avg:active_directory.ldap.successful_binds_persec{*} by {host}, 'agile', 4, direction='both', alert_window='last_15m', interval=120, count_default_zero='true', seasonality='hourly') >= 1

***Added***:

* Add `enable_legacy_tags_normalization` option to preserve hyphens in tag values when set to false. ([#22303](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/22303))
